stories.title: OpenAI reportedly raises another $11B at a $1.25T valuation as it eyes a 2027 IPO
stories.summary:
OpenAI is steering toward a 2027 public debut, and its last private raise is still adding money despite a lowered target.

- OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11B at a $1.25T valuation; the round hasn't closed but is expected to in the coming weeks, per TechCrunch
- The round's target was lowered after it fell short of expectations; it was earlier reported at $30B, with the valuation down from $1.4T in late September
- President Greg Brockman says OpenAI could be IPO-ready in 2027, citing accelerating enterprise revenue and a business turnaround
- Altman has said OpenAI must "be able to make confident safety claims" before going public, tying the IPO to getting its rogue-AI incidents under control, per Gizmodo

stories.title: Meta's Muse adds Spaces and avatar video chat as it passes 10M users amid mounting controversies

- New: Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent, follows avatar video chat for US users and a planned Tamagotchi-like Muse wearable (TechCrunch)
- Meta said on its Q3 earnings call that Muse has over 10 million users; Zuckerberg said a quarter of them shop through the agent, spending about $200 per purchase on average
- Muse hit 10 million US downloads in its first 40 days, a milestone only 11 other apps have reached, and keeps users better than rival AI apps
- Meta suspended Muse's conversation sharing after researchers showed shared links exposed sensitive personal and business data
- Other controversies: OnlyFans creators object to Muse's sexual chat, a since-fixed Mac 0-day, and a contractor "human concierge" reportedly making racist remarks on calls
- Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com; Meta admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw

stories.title: Voters reject AI data centers in the US midterms as the backlash reaches the ballot box
stories.summary:
Public backlash against AI data centers over power costs, water use, land, and environmental justice has now shown up at the ballot box, where voters rejected them in the midterms.

- Americans voted overwhelmingly against data centers, most strongly in Ohio, which flipped blue; voters didn't buy the pitch that the projects boost the economy
- Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market, may lose its lead after Democrats won its Senate seat (James Talarico over Ken Paxton) and governorship (Gina Hinojosa)
- OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to protect grid reliability and consumer electricity costs, and OpenAI may rebrand its data centers as "AI compute campuses"
- Amazon pledged to stop using NDAs with local governments, paired with a warning to critics not to get in the way
- Nearly $200 billion worth of US projects have been blocked or delayed this year; Trump admitted he is a NIMBY on data centers
- Big Tech is countering with a multimillion-dollar ad campaign, a Thiel- and Koch-backed pro-data-center party, and youth outreach like data center field trips
